price.basis: Trek's pre-owned listing of a 2023 Dual Sport+ 2 gives the original price

price.quote: Trek has just released its lowest priced e-bikes in its current range – the Dual Sport+ and the FX+, with the former retailing at $2399 / £2150 and the more urban styled latter at $2499 / £2250. On both e-bikes costs are kept relatively low by using a 250W hub motor with a modest 40Nm torque rating.

cls.basis: 20 mph pedal assist, no throttle = Class 1 (class not stated on maker page)

cls.quote: There are some nice touches as you would expect from Trek, including a frame-integrated battery, small handlebar-mounted display control and best of all from a performance point of view, a torque sensor in the bottom bracket. Range extender batteries are available for both models. They are both 20mph / class 1 pedelecs in the US (Euro spec also available elsewhere) with respective claimed weights of 17.5 and 17.7kg – or both just under 37.5lbs.

notes: Likely discontinued as a new bike, but the maker doesn't say so: the src (electra.trekbikes.com landing page, Trek-owned) still exists but its 'SHOP DUAL SPORT+' link returns 404, and Trek's own search shows only pre-owned Dual Sport+ 2 listings (no new ones). Specs taken from that Trek pre-owned listing (2023 Dual Sport+ 2, Hyena hub) and the landing page. EBR's 'Dual Sport+' review is the 2019 Bosch Active Line Plus version (different bike), not used. EBReport news item covers the Hyena-hub launch. No max load or rider height published.
